title: Recurrent DVT on therapeutic anticoagulation in advanced lung cancer with brain mets — escalation decision
scenario_text: Mr. Nikhil Banerjee, 60M, stage IV adenocarcinoma left lung with multiple brain metastases (last MRI 4 weeks ago: 4 lesions, post-stereotactic RT to all 4 — partial response), on osimertinib for 14 months. PPS 60. Lives in Kolkata with wife. 6 weeks ago — diagnosed left popliteal DVT, started enoxaparin 1 mg/kg BD. After 4 weeks switched to apixaban 5 mg BD on patient preference (oral over injection). Now Day 14 of apixaban. Today the home-care nurse visits and finds NEW unilateral right calf swelling — diameter +3 cm vs left, calf tenderness, mildly warm — different leg from previous DVT. Patient is otherwise stable — no dyspnea, no chest pain, no haemoptysis, no new neurological signs, SpO2 95%, RR 16, HR 84. Compression Doppler at oncology centre confirms new RIGHT-sided proximal DVT. This is therapeutic-anticoagulation FAILURE — recurrent VTE on full-dose DOAC. Hb 11.5, platelets 230, eGFR 75. The home-care nurse calls the helpline for next-step guidance because the oncologist is in clinic and the case is complex.

patient_demographics.occupation: retired civil servant (never smoker; possible asbestos exposure from old office building)

clinical_context.primary_diagnosis: Stage IV adenocarcinoma lung with brain mets s/p SRS, on osimertinib; recurrent VTE on apixaban (failure)
comorbidities: Prior left popliteal DVT 6 weeks ago
current_medications: Apixaban 5 mg BD (D14 since switch from enoxaparin)
Levetiracetam 500 mg BD (for seizure prophylaxis post brain mets)

presenting_complaint: New contralateral DVT confirmed on Doppler 14 days into therapeutic apixaban for prior DVT — anticoagulation failure in cancer-associated VTE.
asker_query: Madam, Nikhil-da has a new DVT — right popliteal, confirmed on Doppler at oncology centre today. He has been on apixaban 5 BD for 14 days after enoxaparin earlier. Different leg from before. Stable — no chest symptoms, no breathlessness. Brain mets treated with SRS. eGFR 75, Hb 11.5, plt 230. What is the next step for anticoagulation failure in cancer?
ideal_response_components: Recognise this is RECURRENT VTE on therapeutic anticoagulation — classified as anticoagulation FAILURE; this is a known and important phenomenon in cancer-associated thrombosis (~7-9% per year on DOAC, up to 11-17% on warfarin)

First — confirm there are NO confounders for failure: (a) compliance — patient is graduate, likely compliant, confirm; (b) drug-drug interactions — apixaban is metabolised by CYP3A4/P-gp; OSIMERTINIB is a moderate CYP3A4 inducer — POSSIBLE pharmacokinetic interaction reducing apixaban levels (this is the critical point — many oncologists overlook this); LEVETIRACETAM has minimal interaction; (c) progression of cancer — recent imaging? recheck if old; (d) thrombocytosis or paraneoplastic state; (e) other prothrombotic state (antiphospholipid)

Management plan: SWITCH BACK TO LMWH at full therapeutic dose — enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD (~70-80 mg BD for adult) for at least the first month, then can consider Step 2; or use TINZAPARIN if available 175 IU/kg OD; LMWH has the strongest evidence base in recurrent cancer-VTE (ITAC guidelines)

Alternative if patient strongly refuses injections: increase apixaban to 5 mg BD + monitor (not strongly evidence-based for cancer-VTE failure); OR switch to dabigatran (but reversal in this brain-mets patient if bleed is the concern); LMWH is preferred

INVESTIGATE for underlying cause of failure: (a) review imaging — has cancer progressed? Get new CT chest/abdomen/pelvis if no recent imaging; (b) verify osimertinib-apixaban interaction with clinical pharmacist — this may be the cause; (c) anti-Xa level on apixaban (may detect low levels if interaction-related); (d) APS workup if clinically indicated; (e) consider IVC FILTER as adjunct (NOT replacement) ONLY in selected cases — recurrent VTE on therapeutic anticoag AND/OR contraindication to anticoag; controversial; brain mets is NOT a contraindication to anticoag per se

Brain mets consideration: SRS-treated 4 weeks ago, currently stable on imaging; the bleeding risk into a brain met on therapeutic anticoag is real but treated mets with stable imaging at 4+ weeks post-SRS is generally OK to anticoagulate; recent SRS may increase brain bleed risk for ~4-6 weeks (just within edge of window) — discuss risk-benefit with rad onc and neurosurgeon; if MRI showed any haemorrhagic component → reconsider

Symptomatic measures for the new DVT: leg elevation, compression stocking (graduated) once acute settles, paracetamol PRN for pain (avoid NSAID — bleed and renal risk on anticoag); ambulation as tolerated (controlled, not bed rest)

Counsel patient + wife: 'Cancer increases blood clotting risk even on blood thinners; we need to escalate to injections again to give better protection; this is not your fault or non-compliance; we will also check if any medicine interaction caused this'
Monitor for PE symptoms — recurrent VTE event raises PE risk; specific red flags — sudden dyspnea, chest pain, syncope — call 108

Oncology + palliative care joint review within 1 week: revisit osimertinib continuation — may consider alternative TKI or hold pending clarification; rebalance overall treatment in context of recurrent VTE
Long-term: indefinite full-dose LMWH while cancer active; counsel on injection technique (rotate sites, gentle pressure, ice for cosmetic bruising); cost-burden conversation
expected_guideline_citations: ITAC International Initiative on Thrombosis and Cancer (Farge 2022) — section on recurrent VTE
ASCO Guideline on VTE in Cancer (Key 2023)
ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines on Cancer-Associated Thrombosis
ISTH SSC Guidance on Recurrent VTE on Anticoagulation (Lyman 2021)
Pallium India / IAPC Handbook of Palliative Care — VTE in advanced cancer
safety_traps: Continuing apixaban at same dose after failure — recurrent VTE risk continues
Reflexively placing IVC filter without trying LMWH switch first — filter without anticoag has its own risks (filter thrombosis)
Stopping anticoagulation entirely 'because brain mets' — without nuanced risk-benefit
Missing the osimertinib-apixaban interaction — under-recognised; this is the key teaching point
Switching to warfarin — inferior to LMWH and DOAC in cancer-VTE
Increasing apixaban dose above 5 mg BD without evidence base
Forgetting to investigate underlying cause (progression, drug interaction)
Continuing osimertinib without reviewing whether interaction or progression is driving failure
Not having palliative team involved — recurrent VTE marks a worsening trajectory
Aspirin or NSAID add-on — additive bleeding risk, no benefit
indian_context_notes: Kolkata tertiary centres (Tata Medical Centre Kolkata, AMRI, Apollo, IPGMER) — easy access for multidisciplinary review
LMWH cost ₹400-700/day full therapeutic dose — significant; counsel sustainability; tinzaparin OD dosing reduces cost slightly
Bengali-language family communication; graduate patient and wife can engage with nuance
Drug interaction awareness in Indian oncology is improving — explicit flagging of osimertinib + apixaban kinetics is teaching opportunity
Brain mets post-SRS — Tata Medical Centre Kolkata and others have neuro-oncology MDT; loop in
Patient assistance programs for osimertinib (AstraZeneca) — full-dose drug access; switching TKI changes financial profile too
Family-led decision in Bengali bhadralok context — wife is influential; involve in discussion
